submitted.rationale: Index 20 (Cr 0.32, Sb 0.68) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0278%. It sits near the trirutile CrSb2O6 composition, which MACE puts close to the hull (0.015 eV/atom). EQE rose steadily with Sb fraction across the three samples: 0.011% at Sb 0.30, 0.021% at Sb 0.48 and 0.028% at Sb 0.68.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0107%. The Cr-rich region (Cr5Sb3O16 / Cr2O3 mix) gave the lowest merit of the three.
Measured EQE 0.0208%, lower than index 20. This is the rutile CrSbO4 region.

consultations.verdict: Support. Rutile CrSbO4 has an HSE gap of about 2.0 eV, which absorbs 3.2 eV light, and sits near the hull (0.065 eV/atom). Index 14 (Sb 0.48) is close to the 1:1 composition. The CrSb2O6 gap prediction (0.96 eV) looks low and less reliable.

Support. The Cr-rich phase Cr5Sb3O16 has a predicted HSE gap of about 2.0 eV, which absorbs 3.2 eV light. The Sb-rich Cr3Sb5O16 gap (0.88 eV) is low and it lies further off the hull (0.107 eV/atom). Index 8 (Sb 0.30) samples the Cr-rich region, away from the modest result at index 14.

Mixed, but I lean toward measuring. MACE puts trirutile CrSb2O6 nearly on the hull (0.015 eV/atom), so it should form as a phase-pure film near Sb 0.67. MEGNet's gap of 0.75 eV looks underestimated for Cr3+ d-d/CT; either way it absorbs 3.2 eV light. The measured trend also rises from Sb 0.30 (0.011%) to Sb 0.48 (0.021%), which supports going Sb-rich.
